This document describes a simple hydrological model of three qa (Shubayqa, Qattafi and Wisad) in the eastern Jordanian Badia.
It has three components:

1. A delineation of the extent of the basins (watersheds) of each qa based on topographic flow analysis
2. Palaeoclimatic reconstructions of the annual precipitation across each of these basins in key periods
3. A simple water balance model used to estimate effective precipitation and by extension the potential volume of water collected in each qa

All three components were implemented in R.
A reproducible research compendium containing the data and code used to perform this analysis, and generate this document, is available at: <https://github.com/joeroe/badia_qa_hydrology>

```{r vars}
data_raw <- path(here(), "analysis", "data", "raw_data")
data_drv <- path(here(), "analysis", "data", "derived_data")

crs_unproj <- 4326
crs_proj <- 32637
```

# Basin delineation

To delineate the basins of each qa, we constructed a hydrological model using WhiteboxTools version 1.4.0 [@Lindsay2016].

```{r data-qa}
st_read(path(data_raw, "badia_qa.gpkg"), layer = "badia_qa") %>% 
  st_transform(qa, crs = crs_proj) %>% 
  mutate(qa = factor(qa, c("Shubayqa", "Qattafi", "Wisad"))) %>% 
  mutate(centroid = st_centroid(geometry)) ->
  qa
```

The starting point was a digital elevation model (DEM) covering the eastern Jordanian *Badia*, extracted from NASADEM 1 arc-second, void-filled global topographic data [@Nasa_jpl2020] and reprojected to UTM zone 37 N.
To prepare the DEM for hydrological modelling, we applied the following standard preprocessing steps:

* Smoothing with Sun et al.'s feature-preserving denoising algorithm [@Sun2007; @Stevenson2010]. 
* Flattening of the area under the three qa under study to a constant elevation
* Filling closed depressions to ensure flow across the entire study region

We traced the visible extent of the modern qa beds from satellite imagery in Google Earth.
Since the DEM was preprocessed to flatten these areas, we can consider the centroid of each qa to be its outlet point for the purposes of the hydrological model.
We then estimated the upslope watersheds of each of these outlet points using the 'simple D8' flow direction algorithm [@OCallaghan1984].
The results are shown in figure \@ref(fig:basin-plot).

## Basin characteristics

```{r basin-summary}
qa %>% 
  mutate(qa_area = st_area(geometry),
         basin_area = st_area(basin)) ->
  qa
```

```{r basin-table, include=TRUE}
qa %>% 
  mutate(qa_area = as.numeric(qa_area) / 1e6,
         basin_area = as.numeric(basin_area) / 1e6) %>% 
  st_set_geometry("centroid") %>% 
  st_transform(crs_unproj) %>% 
  mutate(
    x = st_coordinates(centroid)[,"X"],
    y = st_coordinates(centroid)[,"Y"],
    x = format(round(x, 2), nsmall = 2),
    y = format(round(y, 2), nsmall = 2),
    coordinates = paste0(y, "° N, ", x, "° E")
  ) %>% 
  as_tibble() %>% 
  select(Qa = qa, Coordinates = coordinates, qa_area, basin_area) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  cols_label(qa_area = "Bed area", basin_area = "Basin area") %>% 
  cols_align("left", vars(Qa, Coordinates)) %>% 
  cols_align("right", vars(qa_area, basin_area)) %>% 
  fmt_number(vars(qa_area, basin_area), pattern = "{x} km²")
```

**Shubayqa** drains a large portion of the southeastern slopes of the well-watered Jebel Druze, via Wadi Rajil,
as well as the western slopes of the Tulul al Ashaqif, primarily via Wadi Salma.
It lies on the northern edge of the greater Azraq basin, into which Shubayqa drains via Wadi Rajil.
It is unclear from printed maps and satellite imagery whether the drainage system to the north of the qa—Wadi al-Hashad—lies within the watershed of the Shubayqa/Azraq basin.
Helms [@Helms1981, p. 146] connects it to Wadi Rajil via the Qa Shubayqa, but GIS-based flow direction analysis at multiple scales consistently shows it beyond the watershed, draining north.
Given the relatively flat terrain and poorly developed drainage network of the *Badia* [@Allison2000], combined with the limited resolution of available DEMs, it is possible these models do not fully reflect the reality.
It is also possible that the landforms have changed such that it is no longer connected but was in the past.
If either are the case, the addition of the Wadi al-Hashad drainage would include a much of eastern foothills of the Jebel Druze within the Shubayqa basin.

**Qattafi** and **Wisad** drain slightly larger areas, but in the drier interior of the *Badia*.
They straddle the southern end of the Tulul al Ashaqif: 
Qattafi on the eastern slope, in the Azraq basin; 
Wisad on the western slope, in the Hammad basin.
The wadi systems of these slopes channel a significant portion of the region's rainfall to qa like Qattafi and Wisad [@Al-Qudah2009, p. 605], though presumably at a lesser volume than the Jebel Druze.

# Palaeoclimate

We extracted reconstructed precipitation from downscaled global palaeoclimate simulations [@Fordham2017; @Brown2018] and recent historic climate data [@Karger2017].
The data from PaleoClim includes the mean annual precipitation aggregated over the climate period (fig. \@ref(fig:paleoclim-map)).

```{r data-paleoclim}
# native stars version
# paleoclim <- read_stars(dir_ls(path(data_raw, "paleoclim"), glob = "*.tif"))
# periods <- str_extract(names(paleoclim), "[^_]+")
# biovars <- str_extract(names(paleoclim), "bio_[0-9]+")

tibble(
  path = dir_ls(path(data_raw, "paleoclim"), glob = "*.tif"),
  file = basename(path),
  period = str_extract(file, "[^_]+"),
  biovar = str_extract(file, "bio_[0-9]+"),
  rast = map(path, raster::raster),
  star = map(rast, st_as_stars)
) %>% 
  mutate(
    period = factor(period, 
                    levels = c("HS1", "BA", "YDS", "EH", "MH", "LH", "CHELSA"),
                    labels = c("Heinrich 1", "Bølling-Allerød", "Younger Dryas",
                               "Early Holocene", "Mid Holocene", "Late Holocene",
                               "Present")),
  ) ->
  paleoclim
```

```{r paleoclim-map, include=TRUE, fig.asp=1, fig.cap='Paleoclimate reconstructions of the Badia'}
paleoclim %>% 
  filter(biovar %in% c("bio_12")) %>% 
  mutate(rast = map(rast, raster::as.data.frame, xy = TRUE)) %>% 
  mutate(rast = map(rast, set_names, nm = c("x", "y", "value"))) %>% 
  unnest(rast) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, z = value)) +
  geom_contour_filled(breaks = c(0, 50, 100, 150, 200, 300, 400, 500)) +
  scale_fill_carto_d(palette = "Teal") +
  facet_wrap(vars(period), ncol = 3, strip.position = "top") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Annual precipitation (mm)") +
  coord_sf(crs = crs_proj, expand = FALSE) +
  fixed_plot_aspect() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank()
  )
```

We used this data to calculate the precipitation across each of the qa basins (fig. \@ref(fig:paleoclim-qa-summary-plot)).

```{r paleoclim-qa}
paleoclim %>% 
  filter(biovar == "bio_12") %>% 
  select(period, star) %>% 
  mutate(star = map(star, st_warp, crs = crs_proj)) ->
  paleoclim_subset

qa %>% 
  slice(rep(1:n(), each = nrow(paleoclim_subset))) %>% 
  bind_cols(slice(paleoclim_subset, rep(1:n(), times = nrow(qa)))) %>% 
  group_by(qa) %>% 
  mutate(prec = map(star, `[`, basin)) %>% 
  select(-star) %>% 
  ungroup() ->
  qa
```

```{r paleoclim-qa-summary}
# Cell area in m^2
paleoclim_res <- abs(st_dimensions(qa$prec[[1]])[["x"]]$delta * st_dimensions(qa$prec[[1]])[["y"]]$delta)

qa %>% 
  mutate(prec = map(prec, as.data.frame)) %>% 
  mutate(prec = map(prec, set_names, nm = c("x", "y", "prec"))) %>% 
  unnest(prec) %>% 
  drop_na(prec) %>% 
  group_by(period, qa) %>% 
  summarise(
    qa_area = first(qa_area),
    basin_area = first(basin_area),
    prec_avg = mean(prec),
    prec_total = sum(prec), # i.e. mm across ncells
    ncells = n(),
    prec_volume = sum(prec * paleoclim_res) / 1000, # In m^3
    .groups = "drop_last"
  ) ->
  qa_summary
```

```{r paleoclim-qa-summary-plot, include=TRUE, fig.asp=1, fig.cap='Reconstructed precipitation across the qa basins for key climate periods'}
p_prec1 <- qa_summary %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = period, y = prec_avg, group = qa)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = qa), filter(qa_summary, period == "Present")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean annual precipitation (mm)") +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

p_prec2 <- qa_summary %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = period, y = prec_volume / 1e6, group = qa)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = qa), filter(qa_summary, period == "Present")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Total precipitation (million m^3)") + 
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

p_prec1 / p_prec2
```

# Water availability

Estimating the volume of this rainfall that actually reached the qa requires a water balance model.
Unfortunately, there is practically no data available that could be used to constrain such a model in this region.
As a first order of approximation, we therefore adopted the simple equation used by Whitehead et al. [-@Whitehead2008] for Jawa, defining effective precipitation ($P_E$, in mm) as:

$$P_E = K(P-E)$$

Where $P$ is total precipitation (mm), $E$ is rainfall lost to evapotranspiration (mm) and $K$ is the proportion of rainfall that enters the wadi system (allowing for infilitration).
We also follow Whitehead et al. in estimating the values of the constants $K$ and $E$ at 0.03±0.01 and 30±20 mm respectively.
Applying this model to the qa basins, we can estimate the volume of water that reached them in each climate period.

To further estimate the volume potentially retained in the qa, we calculated the volume of the qa.
To do this we assume they are an oblate hemispheroid, with the product of the major semi-axes ($a^2$) equal to the area of the modern qa bed, and the length of the minor semi-axis ($b$) equal to the minimum depth established by our sediment dating (see main Table 2).
The volume is then:

$$V=\frac{2}{3}\pi a^2 b$$

```{r water-table, include=TRUE}
tribble(
  ~qa,        ~period,           ~depth,
  "Qattafi",  "Heinrich 1",      0.95,
  "Qattafi",  "Bølling-Allerød", 0.95,
  "Qattafi",  "Younger Dryas",   0.95,
  "Qattafi",  "Early Holocene",  0.95,
  "Qattafi",  "Mid Holocene",    0.6,
  "Qattafi",  "Late Holocene",   NA,
  "Qattafi",  "Present",         NA,
  "Wisad",    "Heinrich 1",      1.45,
  "Wisad",    "Bølling-Allerød", 1.45,
  "Wisad",    "Younger Dryas",   1.45,
  "Wisad",    "Early Holocene",  0.65,
  "Wisad",    "Mid Holocene",    0.65,
  "Wisad",    "Late Holocene",   NA,
  "Wisad",    "Present",         NA,
  "Shubayqa", "Heinrich 1",      1.95,
  "Shubayqa", "Bølling-Allerød", 1.95,
  "Shubayqa", "Younger Dryas",   1.95,
  "Shubayqa", "Early Holocene",  1.95,
  "Shubayqa", "Mid Holocene",    1.37,
  "Shubayqa", "Late Holocene",   1.15,
  "Shubayqa", "Present",         NA
) %>% 
  right_join(qa_summary, by = c("qa", "period")) %>% 
  # Water balance model
  mutate(k = 0.03, k_error = 0.01, e = 30, e_error = 20,
         eff_prec_low = (k - k_error) * (prec_total - ((e + e_error) * ncells)),
         eff_prec_high = (k + k_error) * (prec_total - ((e - e_error) * ncells)),
         eff_prec_volume_low = (eff_prec_low * paleoclim_res) / 1000,
         eff_prec_volume_high = (eff_prec_high * paleoclim_res) / 1000) %>% 
  # Qa volume & percentage filled
  mutate(qa_volume = as.numeric((2/3 * pi * qa_area * depth)),
         filled_low = eff_prec_volume_low / qa_volume,
         filled_high = eff_prec_volume_high / qa_volume) %>% 
  select(qa, period, depth, qa_volume, 
         eff_prec_volume_low, eff_prec_volume_high,
         filled_low, filled_high) %>% 
  group_by(qa) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  cols_label(period = "Period", depth = "Depth (m)", 
             qa_volume = "Volume (m³)", 
             eff_prec_volume_low = "Effective precipitation (m³)",
             filled_low = "Volume filled") %>% 
  cols_merge_range(vars(eff_prec_volume_low), vars(eff_prec_volume_high)) %>% 
  cols_merge_range(vars(filled_low), vars(filled_high)) %>% 
  fmt_percent(vars(filled_low, filled_high)) %>% 
  fmt_missing(everything(), missing_text = "—")
```
